When I first opened this shirt, I was immediately impressed with the quality. It reminds me of a eco-friendly boutique type garment. It's a good thickness and much nicer than a lot of basic t-shirts out there.

My 20 year old daughter wanted something like this for yoga and exercise. The fabric is much nicer than I expected. It's soft, but it's also pretty thick. It's not see through at all. Of course, you can see the lines of garments worn underneath, but you can't see the designs and colors. The sizing was as expected. There's a good amount of stretch in the leggings. The bra looked small, but it did fit my daughter fine. She's a 34D. It doesn't offer much support though. She says it will be fine for yoga, but she won't be able to jog or run in it without wearing another bra underneath.

I finally got it unfolded, but it didn't seem very smooth like it had a crease in it or something. The bralette doesn't offer a whole lot of support. I would not wear this in public, but for lounging at home, it's perfect! The straps are not adjustable. Overall, I am satisfied with it.

First off, I'm a woman with larger hands so it's difficult to find decent gloves that both fit my hands and that are also stylish ('cause let's be honest, it's always nice for gloves to not only do their job but look good doing it). Well, I stumbled across these and decided to give 'em a go. Man am I glad I did!

They were delivered quickly which was very much appreciated given a heavy storm.. perfect timing. That storm presented me with the opportunity to put them to the test immediately.

I purchased the large and they fit my larger hands, well.. like a glove. I couldn't ask for a better fit. I usually get gloves that are either 1) too small (most gloves I try) where the stitching for the web between my fingers is at least an inch above my actual web so I find myself always pushing them down which causes the stitching to give out prematurely.. or 2) too large (whenever I wear my husband's gloves) where the stitching comes down to my web but the fingers are too long and I have at least an inch (usually closer to two inches) sticking out beyond the tips of my fingers which causes me to drop anything I might try to pickup. Needless to say, finding the perfect gloves has been a long, seemingly endless battle for me.

But these gloves! Oh yes! They fit! They are so soft inside and out and the color is a nice neutral color that goes with practically anything. The stitching meets my web, there is no excess material extending past my finger tips and they are lined with some of the softest fleece I've ever felt.

Back to the storm.. I wore these gloves while we bucked about a 1/2 cord of firewood. It was cold (14F, 3F with wind chill) and wet as the wood pile had snow from a previous storm on it and it was beginning to snow again. So these gloves kept my hands comfortably warm.. even after they became visibly soaked. Since they are not specifically described as waterproof, I wasn't sure how they'd hold up to the wet snow but they ended up drying out and, other than being a little dirty, looked like they just came out of the packaging.

Their stitching is impressive. There are no uncomfortable bumps or lumps that some gloves tend to have along the fingers or fingertips and the stitching around the thumb and in the palm area is very well done and appears it will survive what I need to ask of them.

Bottom line... I highly recommend these gloves! I do believe they will withstand our infamously harsh Wyoming Winters, so they should be good for you too!

I own a number of Booq products, so when I was offered a review sample of this new model I accepted. Like all Booq bags the emphasis is on efficient management of space as well as protecting electronics. This bag is no exception.

First, unlike the other bags that I own this one is kind of complicated, In fact, the shoulder strap and stabilizer strap design drove me crazy at first. Even the instruction card was of little help. Basically I had problems grasping how the magnetic buckle and stabilizing straps were designed for, as well as the fact that the shoulder pad on the strap hid the magnetic buckle when I first unboxed it. I finally figured it out with patience and carefully studying the diagrams.

Second, at first I thought the shoulder and stabilizer straps were poorly designed. I was wrong. They are designed for perfect ergonomics and balance. Again, this is a learning curve issue. In some ways Booq has been too clever in the design because there is a complexity that takes time to learn. For me it's worth it because I can carry a relatively heavy load (about thirty pounds) in a balanced fashion and still be assured that the tablet and a few other electronic odds and ends I carry are well protected. Protection is one area where Booq excels.

This is not trendy fine leather. Vegans will love it, and while I do not know exactly what it is, it's some sort of durable plastic material that is superbly constructed. The stitching, webbing, clasps and zippers are all first rate. Water literally rolls off it, and the reflective piping is a nice touch with respect to safety, whether walking or cycling.

Organizational options and features are another Booq hallmark. Instead of my trying to describe them in detail, look at the product photos on this page. There is a place for everything, and it has been well thought out. I've had this bag for a week and am still discovering compartments.

Bottom line: this is a bag that does take time to learn. It probably should come with a video or a link to one, which will make it immediately useful because I can assure you that the first day of ownership will be frustrating. Take your time and learn it because after that you will love it totally.

I replenish the socks often as they are not meant to last forever (the sock may hold up but the compression decreases over time). SO I am always on the look out for a decent compression sock. These are NOT IT. I will tell you why:

The compression on these is about right. No real complaint there. Very important to select a size based not only on your foot size, but also on your calf size. If deciding between the two, I would aim for calf size or go to a different brand.

They are thin in calf area. I sense these will lose compression sooner over later.

One sock has a hole it in it that I noticed as I put it on. A hole with a run! No good! Also, if that weren't bad enough..

One sock is way too long. It goes up over my knee nearly to my thigh. The other sock just goes to my knee (as it should). The socks SHOULD fit in such a manner that it goes to the knee, or just below. Not so far above that it is like a thigh sock. Makes them uncomfortable as the band will bite the skin.

Maybe I just got a bad pair or maybe there is a bad batch. Regardless, I am disappointed. I CAN wear them, but again they have a hole and one is uncomfortably long. '

To end on a positive, the foot is accurate for sizing. I have size 10/11 womens (8/9 mens) and the L/XL is suitable for womens size 8/12.5 and mens 8-14. I have room left over. Just also need to have a calf size within 14-19 range. My measurement is around 17"

The foot has a slightly padded feel.
Toe seam sits on top of toes and not at toe nail (which is good thing)
Since there are so many design and color change, then know that there are corresponding threads on the inside. This is a not a positive but it isnt necessarily negative either.. it is just a detail I find worth mentioning as it may mean that some people may catch a toenail on the interior threads.

If my sock didnt have a hole in it (and a run) and if the socks were the same length ending at or just below knee, I would have rated these a 4. But with the host of problems I can't recommend these nor will I ever purchase more from this brand.

--I like these big sunglasses. I have them in purple. I wouldn't really notice them being purple. A greyish-blackish-purplishlens

-- I can wear them driving or just out and about outside, and everything without issue. I notice that they have a gradient lens. --Comes with a soft shell zippered hard case with lens cloth.

--I noticed though, that when I try to look at my smartphone with these on, there is a prism effect. It is very odd. --of the color choices available it appears that black, red, and purple all have a dark lens, while the brown pair has an amber looking lens. I imagine that alters how things look. Just keep that in mind when making a selection, or seek out reviews based on the color you are considering.

This is my second Befen wallet. I have not been disappointed at all. I LOVED my first one (which I reviewed, and it is still in good condition, just wanted something with a strap) and this one is just as wonderful. I LOVE it. The structural integrity of the product is refreshingly impressive. It is large enough to carry basic needs, but not at all bulky. I can carry my LGv20 (with a case!) inside, though a tight fit. The zippers are solid and strong. The stitching is solid. Clasps are strong. I'm not gentle with my stuff and this wallet can handle it. With so much junk out there, it is once again nice to be able to buy and use a product that I am truly impressed with. The material does not hold a stain-- just a quick wipe to keep it clean.
If I could make one minor adjustment, it would be to make the shoulder strap a little longer. The strap is already adjustable (like a belt). It works well for over the shoulder, and it works as a cross body wallet if on the last notch. For me, being tall, a couple more inches worked in would allow the cross body option to sit at a lower and less awkward length. Since most people are likely smaller than me, then I expect the max length to work fine. I will say, that I have gotten creative with the wrist strap by attaching the larger strap to that to give me 4-5 extra inches in length when needed as a cross body wallet. I plan to buy another in a different color. Please please please keep up the great quality.

We always help her take them off or put them on though. These have a lot of force and if her hands were to slip during grasping them they would snap together with quite some force. Overall, these are a great pair of noise reducing earmuffs and my daughter enjoys wearing them.

These compression socks are manufactured right here in the good old USA! Kudos to this company for not outsourcing!

These knee-high socks are 15-20 mmHg, mild-compression socks, which is no doubt why they are labeled as primarily travel socks. People who have specific health issues usually choose socks with a higher level of compression than these. I myself wear compression socks because I stand or walk up to 12 hours a day, and compression socks at this level of compression successfully prevent tired and sore feet, shin splints and cramps in my calves.

The fabric in these socks, which is Polyester/Spandex, is very soft and, as advertised, it is stretchy enough to make it much easier to put these socks on than many other brands of compression socks. But even so, these socks are not so stretchy that it compromises firm support.

I love the feel of this fabric. It is so smooth and comfy, it is a pleasure both to put on these socks and to wear them. I don't think I've ever felt fabric of this high quality in any compression socks I've ever worn, and I've tried out at least eight different brands at this point.

Note that these are casual socks rather than dress socks. The compression socks I own which are sold as dress socks are made of a lighter-weight fabric than these. These socks might be a bit too heavyweight to be worn at the height of summer in a situation without air conditioning.

The top of these socks is designed in such a way that it stays firmly in place, without drooping, while avoiding being so tight it impedes blood circulation.

The heel and toe of these socks are reinforced, but they do not poke or bind my toes.

The sizing on these socks is accurate. I ordered the size I normally wear, and it fits perfectly.

These socks are available in multiple fashion designs and colors to suit many different tastes. They can be purchased as a single pair, which is the case with these particular socks, or in a 3-pack with a variety of designs among the several pairs of socks.

While it is possible to wash these socks in a washing machine and put them in the dryer, I would never do that myself, because that amount of rigorous handling will cause them to wear out much, much sooner. Instead, I hand wash all of my compression socks in warm water with mild soap, rinse them well, gently squeeze out excess water, and hang them up to dry. Given that these socks are black, I place an old towel beneath them to catch the several, inevitable drips of black dye so that they don't stain my tub.

I love kickboxing--in fact, it's one of the few forms of cardio that I truly enjoy. Unfortunately, I found this DVD to be disappointing. The moves themselves were fun and the combinations were mostly interesting, but I did not click at all with the teaching style of the instructor, Ilaria Montagnani. In this workout, Ilaria teaches very LONG combinations of punches and kicks. Although she teaches in an "add-on" style, starting with a few moves and then adding on new moves, each time she goes back to the beginning, she does NOT cue the moves! For example, she will simply say "let's start again," and then the reviewer is expected to recall all the moves up to that point WITHOUT Ilaria saying what they are. This is made even more difficult by the camera angles--e.g., sometimes the camera is focusing on Ilaria from the waist up only, so you can't see the kicks that she is doing.

If each combination was short and repeated many times, this might not be such an issue, but as noted above, the combos are quite lengthy. I have described each below. To make matters worse, the combinations are DIFFERENT on each side of the body--in her Introduction, Ilaria says that this does not matter, as you will be doing about the same number of punches and kicks, but it definitely felt uneven to me. All times listed are approximately.

WARM-UP (5 minutes)
Mostly alternating punches front, including jab, cross punch, hook, and upper cut. The front push kick is included as well, but no other kicks are practiced in the warm-up. I set of push-ups is performed at the end.

PUNCHES (7 minutes)
Here Ilaria introduces a long punch combination. The combination is performed for many sets (12-16?) on one side, then repeated on the second side. These are the punches (slashes denote where each piece is added on):
jab-jab-cross / hook-cross / upper-cross / fast 3 right-fast 3 left / jab-cross

KICKS (10.5 minutes)
This was more drills than combinations and was easier to follow. Ilaria begins with a front chamber/front kick. Next is a side chamber/roundhouse, building up to three roundhouse kicks. The third kick was the crescent, starting with alternating knees to the side and then adding in the crescent. Finally, the side kick was performed with a chamber/side kick, then moving on to a double knee/side kick/squat.

COMBINATION #1, LEFT SIDE (6.5 minutes)
knee-double front push kick / opposite knee crescent / walk around, opposite knee roundhouse / squat-roundhouse-knee / double roundhouse / jab-cross hook-cross upper-cross

COMBINATION #2, RIGHT SIDE (6 minutes)
jab-jab-cross / front push kick, 2x / opposite leg crescent / walk around, opposite leg roundhouse / squat, roundhouse x3

COMBINATION #3, face forward (10 minutes)
hi level block to side / mid level block to side / alternating sides with side kicks / karate punches

STRETCH (3 minutes)
This is a very brief segment that includes a low back release, a lunge for the hip flexors, a standing side stretch/backbend, and a standing triceps stretch. It did not feel adequate given the overall length of the workout (over 50 minutes).

I actually liked the moves in Combo #3 the most, but I also found this combination to be the MOST frustrating! Ilaria's cuing seemed almost totally random here, as I could never figure out which side she was going to next; I don't think she worked the sides evenly at all. It didn't help that the music sometimes would drown her out (and on top of that, I found her accent sometimes difficult to understand as well). I will say that Ilaria DID give excellent form pointers throughout the workout. Personally, however, I wish she would have spent more time actually cuing the moves themselves.

The main pro about these pants is the fabric. It's soft, comfortable and, despite it being 'pre-aged' it remains decently sturdy. The stitching throughout is also well-done.

However, the list of cons is a bit longer. The overall sizing is unusual. Only one measurement (waist) is provided which usually means the length is the same. Not in this case -- I received a 34 waist but a 30 length, which is well short of what would fit.

Length aside, the overall cut is not to my taste at all. The rise is very short, making these rather uncomfortable to wear. The relaxed fit is mainly in the seat area, and the combination of a short rise and a large seat makes them look ill-fitting (in addition to feeling that way as well).

I'll give it 2 stars since the material is nice, but these are not pants I would recommend even if you need 34 waist and 30 length.

I am a major Taylor Swift fan so when I saw these necklaces I knew I had to have them. I received both the Mastermind and the All Too Well versions. I love both of them. The writing on them is clear and crisp. They look really nice and the clasps work perfectly. I love wearing a little nod to my favorite artist.

What a pretty necklace. It came in this nice zippered pouch. Looks like a change purse. The necklace is very unique looking which is what I liked about it. When I put it on it sits just below my neckline so it is a nice length. I think it is something that I will wear often.

These are cute panties in general but especially for your period. These will be worn on lighter flows days as I prefer my entire nether region to be covered. Overall they actually fit unlike some other plus size period panties tried.
These are too small! They don't fit and I actually ordered a half size larger than needed.  The slippers are cute but what does it even matter if they don't even fit.

I got this bracelet for my SIL since she's on blood thinners.  She has a skinny wrist so we had to bend it some to get it to where it wouldn't fall off.  It's made of very good metal and was hard to bend.  It still looks very good after bending and nothing is lopsided about it.  The print, "Blood Thinner" is pretty small but I'm sure medical personnel would see it.  I think this is a very good bracelet as it's not big and clunky and looks like a jewelry bracelet.
This assortment of sterling silver small hoop earrings are very pretty, but thin.  These would look very nice for multiple piercings.

This is a lovely men's shirt.  It's great for summer wear since it's light weight.  I ordered the XXL size for review and it's pretty much true to size.  I like that the inside, where the buttons are on one side, and the button holes on the other are sewn down.  That way there's no loose or open material to deal with like some cheaper shirts have.  I washed it with like colors using warm water and it went through the wash cycle just fine.  It came out of the dryer somewhat wrinkled, and will need ironing before wearing, but I don't think it shrunk or faded any.  I think this is a very nice shirt and is a beautiful color.

These are very soft and well made men's swim trunks.  They washed well in the regular laundry cycle and came out of the dryer with no noticeable shrinking or fading.  They have built-in mesh underwear to keep the "boys" in place and a cord around the waist for adjustment.  They look exactly as pictured and as of now I can't find anything negative to say about them.  These should be just fine for swimming in.

I just love these sunglasses.  They are very well made, and do a great job at cutting down on sun glare.  I have a narrow head and these fit nicely and they don't bother the bridge of my nose.  They look awesome and I love wearing them.  They come in a very unique bamboo case.

I received 2 pairs of these shorts - a size 12 and a size 14 so I am combining the two into one review.  I'm 5'9", 142 lbs and have an average sized butt.  The 12's were a tad too tight so I gave them to my daughter.  The 14's fit nicely and I'm definitely keeping those.  I washed both pairs in the regular laundry cycle and both pairs came out of the dryer rolled up at the legs which I find a bit frustrating.  They are already short enough (just barely long enough to keep the cellulite hidden) and even when I tried unrolling them they still wanted to roll right back up.  I docked a star for this.  Otherwise, they seem to be well made jeans, are soft and not overly distressed.

I love this tennis skirt leggings combo.  I play a lot of tennis and like to wear leggings under my tennis skirt in cool and cold weather.  This tennis skirt legging combo works out great.  The skirt is lovely, stretchy and made out of very good material and the leggings are made out of the same material.  It's very comfortable and this is my first choice on cold tennis days.  It washes super easy and basically comes out of the dryer wrinkle-free.

This poncho wrap looks a lot better on the product page than it does in real life.  It doesn't fit me well - I'm 5'9", 142 lbs, 34B and I though it would hang a lot better.  It needs to be a little longer and I just can't seem to get it adjusted so that it looks like the picture.  It's thin and not for cold weather unless you have something substantial on underneath it.  The fringe string is really cheap looking and I might find better fringe at the cloth store to replace it later.  As a matter of fact, I think I will sew it up like a real poncho and see if that helps it to hang better on me.  Thank God mom taught me how to sew. I am blown away by the quality and fit of this beautiful blouse.  I received the medium size for review and it fits me just right with a little room to spare.  I'm 5'9". 142 lbs, 34B, and have birthing hips.  This blouse draped nicely over my hips fit well on my shoulders and everything about it was just right.  The material is soft, sheeny with lovely furrows and the sewing is very well done.  There is absolutely nothing negative I can find to say about it.  I placed it in a mesh bag when put in the laundry and placed it on a rack to dry.  It dried beautifully with no wrinkles and looks brand new.  This is a lovely top to wear to even the fancy occasions as well as a casual office top.

I received the medium size dress for review and it fits but is kind of snug.  I'm 5'9", 142 lbs, 34B, have female birthing hips and long arms.  The sleeves were too short, and it went around my hips but kind of snug.  The material is soft and sleeky and is a nice color.  I doubt I will be wearing this dress simply because I just don't feel comfortable in it.  I need a Large size for a better fit.

This is a very pretty necklace but you will have to take some time to make sure the inner and outer chains are not twisted together and that the necklace hangs evenly on your neck. These are very good quality socks to wear in most any casual shoe, especially tennis shoes.  They are well knitted and I like the color banded tops. These are nice and stretchy tights and are perfect for ballet or just to wear with a skirt.  They seem to be very durable and  are easy to wash by placing them in a mesh bag and then into the washing machine.  I hang them up to dry.

The material is very soft but the dress is thin and a long slip must definitely be worn underneath it if you don't want "see - thru". I washed it in the regular dark laundry cycle and it came out of the dryer with no noticeable shrinking or fading.  This dress is something I would wear to a casual event - office, shopping, maybe church but not to a formal event.

This necklace is definitely cheap looking.  It looks like one you would see hanging on the rack next to the cash register in one of those discount Asian stores. I don't know if it will permanently stay attached to the chain or not.  Don't give this to your girlfriend as a serious gift or she will see how cheap you are.

[[VIDEOID:e0c9dc118a0de3ad5f03f9890085a580]]I received this case from the manufacturer for evaluation during the product's launch, and here are my thoughts.

This sturdy leather key holder looks and feels very well constructed. Made of thick vintage looking crazy horse leather, the case is immaculately stitched, has a smoothly functioning zipper, and is about the right size for a man to comfortably carry in a pocket without being overly bulky. There's a sturdy brass hook on the top of the case to hook to a belt, but I used it for my car key instead since I would have to leave the case unzipped when the key was in the ignition if I stored it inside the case.

The inside of the case has two slots to hold gas or other cards, a car key holder in case you prefer to keep your key inside the case, and 6 hooks to hold other keys. Credit cards fit into the slots well, all hooks are brass and feel very secure, and the keys are easy to put on or take off as needed. Overall, it's a nice looking case that appears to be well constructed, but I'd suggest keeping your house key on the inside ring rather than your car key.

I received this charm from the manufacturer at no cost for evaluation during the product's launch, and here are my observations.

This heart shaped charm looks as lovely in person as it does on the product page. Set in brightly polished stamped S925 sterling silver, the charm features a ruby red crystal heart centerpiece surrounded by clear diamond-like crystals, a small clear crystal on the top, and an opening through the heart that's wide enough to fit Pandora style bracelets.

The charm measures 0.4" x 0.4" and it looks lovely on my Pandora style snake chain bracelet. I especially like the fact that the design is done on both sides of the charm so that it is visible regardless of the way the charm is strung on a bracelet or necklace. Silver does tarnish, but it just takes a little bit of care to keep it looking its best. Avoid swimming with the charm on, store it in an air tight pouch when you aren't planning to wear it for a while, and wipe it off with the included silver cloth to keep it looking bright and shiny.

[[VIDEOID:5fe08120129044defabea18feea15ca3]] [[VIDEOID:a8c398caf3412f6f68f3e09e786fbdb7]] I received this bracelet directly from the manufacturer at no cost for evaluation during the product's launch, and here are my observations.

This platinum plated stamped 925 sterling silver bracelet is smooth, brightly polished and beautiful with its sparkling cubic zirconia encrusted bead shaped snap clasp closure. It's beautiful enough to be worn without adding any charms at all, but it does have the same diameter as a Pandora bracelet, so any charm that fit a Pandora bracelet will fit this one as well, and unlike a plain sterling silver bracelet, this one won't ever tarnish.

To open the clasp, you push your nail into the crack on the sparkling snap clasp bead, and it pops right open. I keep my nails on the shorter side, so this isn't a problem for me. Once you add beads to your bracelet be sure to add a bead stopper or a clip charm to keep your beads from dropping off when you open the bracelet. To close the bracelet again just insert the end and push the clasp back together over the end, but don't stop until you hear it click shut. Once it has clicked shut it is very secure and even tugging on the bracelet won't make it pop open.

This tote in blue is absolutely gorgeous, and I love the soft buttery feel of the split leather it's made of. I'm 5'8" tall, and this tote is just the right size for me to carry, not too large and not too small. It's just the right size to carry my iPad plus a couple of spiral notebooks, an infusion bottle, and everything I need to take with me to classes. I begin my internship this coming summer and this tote will help enhance my professional appearance quite nicely.

I love how versatile this tote is. The short handles are rounded nicely for comfort when carrying it by hand, and the longer handles let me carry it over the crook of my arm, but what I really love best about this tote (besides it's appearance) is the fact that I can detach the longer handles entirely when I want to carry the tote as a shoulder bag! I prefer to carry shoulder bags, and this one comes with a detachable strap that adjusts long enough to carry it as a shoulder or cross body bag.

In addition to plenty of storage space and compartments inside the bag itself, there are two zippered storage compartments on the outside of the bag as well, a vertical one in front that's convenient for stashing my car keys and other small items, and a long deep pocket on the back big enough for my passport, boarding passes, or other items I'd prefer to keep right next to my body. All of the zippers open and close smoothly, both compartments are nicely lined, and that back compartment is large enough to even fit an iPad mini.

The main compartment of the tote has full zippered closure, and the interior is lined in a lovely brown fabric decorated in a hearts and flowers pattern. The spacious interior is divided into three sections by a zippered center compartment. Deep enough to hold a standard iPad or small tablet, with room left over for clutch and notebooks, there are two open sleeves for cell phone and another gadget on the wall of the front compartment, and a zippered compartment on the back wall of the rear compartment. Despite it's reasonable size, this tote offers plenty of storage capacity.

I'm very well satisfied with the workmanship and quality of this tote. All seams are impeccably stitched, and the hardware is actually sturdy metal rather than plastic, and nicely done in a silver tone that complements the color of the leather nicely. I really love how it looks and feels. In summary, if you're in the market for an attractive leather tote that's affordably priced this one is a good option. Sure, it's split leather rather than full grain, but for the price, this tote offers a very affordable way to get the look of high end leather without the exorbitant cost.

Y'know, for the money...? I think this is a really great hat. I've had nicer hats, but they cost literally 3 to 4 times more, and they ultimately didn't last me all that long anyways since I seem to just destroy hats quickly. I think because I'm really tall, they get snagged up in branches and stuff quickly. As such, I asked myself "why spend more on a hat that I'm probably gonna destroy or lose in a year, when I can just buy several less-expensive hats?" Well, this is that hat.

The materials are pretty decent. It's not really water resistant, but it'll keep rain out of your face. The mesh will allow good airflow, but keep bugs out. So far, after half a season, I see no evidence of deterioration due to HEAVY UV exposure. The material absorbs sweat fair enough, and can be gently hand washed clean. So far, it's held up to being snagged in three branches, and survived my storage compartment in my SUV. For the money, I think the materials are pretty good.

I was impressed at the build quality, for such an inexpensive hat. The stitching was clean and straight, without any loose threads. All the components were assembled well, leading to a perfectly symmetrical hats (one of my more expensive hats can't say that).

For the money, I got a hat that should probably have cost 2x more. Honestly, I think it even rivals a hat I have that cost nearly 3x more, as far as build quality. It's not as rugged as my even-more-expensive hats, but it doesn't have to - it's as good as I need it to be, and for a lot less money. My only problem is that it's just a little small. It sits a little higher on top of my ginormous pumpkin head than I would like, but so do my other hats. I just have an abnormally large dome - that's a me problem, not the fault of the manufacturer (I assume). It oughtta fit perfectly for most everyone else. Good hat for the money... I recommend it.

I've had a few F91W series watches, and they've all been reliable.  They're so inexpensive, and run so long on the original batteries, they're pretty much disposable.  Over the years, I've bought several of these watches - not to wear on my wrist, but to strap them to my backpack, mount on my bike, and keep in my camp packs. Or, rather, I ~tried~ to put it onto my wrist, but it didn't fit.  I'm not Lou Ferigno or The Big Show, and I could barely touch the tip of the strap to the very tip of the buckle.  I compared it to my older F91W, and it too had a small strap.  A no-name watch from Hong Kong with another "standard men's strap" was a good centimeter longer.  It's not a problem for me, since I don't plan on wearing it, but it's something to keep in mind when purchasing this watch.  As a timepiece, the F91W-1 still great.  Accurate, rugged, water resistant, inexpensive and very plain looking.  I'll trust my life to it as a timepiece, but apparently I won't be wearing them unless I buy a new strap.

These are good little watches and I have been using them since they came out 20-30 years ago. I am not sure if the model number has changed but the simple basic Casio digital watch has always been long lasting and dependable. They are not expensive but have served me well. But from a display standpoint it could be better. Although the display is common with all of these style watches, the illumination button is useless. It does not produce enough light or at the correct angle to read the numbers. I since have started using the Casio F-105 Illuminator, same basic watch but with an outstanding back light feature.

Had an issue with return, too.  Ordered two different colors of this set, and they arrived in the same box.  Set up the same return for both pairs, and sent them back in the box they arrived in, both return slips in the box with them.  Of course, I could only use one of the outside shipping labels.  Come to find out, they don't open the boxes to receive each item.  They simply scan the outer label and put the unopened returned package aside.  Refunded me for only one pair and it took some back and forth on my part to get the refund for the other pair, as they had to locate the box in the warehouse and verify the other pair was returned.  It was refunded, but it was a pain.

I went with the medium in this bra. The cup pads I would normally remove but they add a bit more support so I left them in when working out. The medium fit fairly well at first.

I have worn this bra for strength training and a 30 minute cardio workout on the elliptical. After the elliptical (which is not much bounce) I noticed the bra was sagging and I could have benefited from adjustable straps (this bra does not have that) to make the fit better. I suppose I could sew it to shorten the straps, but not sure I want to mess with that. I will probably just wear the bra for strength training ( low impact) or around the house, because it is comfortable for that.

I started biking on weekends 4 months ago. I'm up to 30 mile rides per day and moved from a mountain bike to a road bike. I needed something to help pad my sensitive areas. These work great and are reasonably priced, too. I noticed a few other reviewers commenting on the quality of the sewing, but I've had no issue with these at all. I wash them on "hand wash" setting in cold water, with woolite in my washing machine. Then I hang them to dry and they are ready for me the next weekend. These classic shorts took about 3 rides before I felt they were "broken in" to my body, but maybe that was just me getting used to these since it's my first time with them. I liked them that I ordered a second pair in the royal blue. But beware- if you sweat a lot the lighter colors dont really hide the sweat. So after wearing the royal blue for 30 mile ride it looks like I peed myself! hahaha.. not a big deal if you're not planning on getting off the bike until you get back home or to your car headed for home. I'm a little self-concious about it so I'll probably just wear the royal blue ones under loose shorts or leggings when the weather is cool.

And for those of you ladies wondering, bike shorts like this are designed to be worn without underwear. Once I learned that they became much more comfy as well!

For an additional $10 you can by the [[ASIN:B004R05P3Q Women's Pro Bike Short Padded for Cycling - Made in USA]] which I find more comfortable than these. The padding is not as stiff and it seems to conform to my body much better which makes it more comfortable for the ride.

overall I'd recommend these shorts if you're on a budget, but if you want a better fit and feel spend the extra $10 and get the pro style.

A recent embrace of style had spurred the realization that my sock collection was rather blasÃ©, consisting mostly of hard-worn gold-toe fluffies and other generic socks. Esteemed sock manufacturer, James Fiallo, rectified my issues by providing this convenient 12 pack assortment of startlingly interesting socks. The patterns are colorful, as indeed claimed, but also tasteful and I've received more complements than snickers (not that it would stop me, anyway) upon donning myself of the aforementioned footwear. There are plenty of colors to match with different colored pants and shoes, several blacks and blues along with many mid-hue green/orange/yellow and several purple colors as well. Socks are an average thickness, but closer to dress socks than athletic socks, not for working out, only for style. They provide just about no warmth, so prepare some warm shoes if you are prone to cold feet (in the empirical, as opposed to metaphorical, sense). My only other complaint is that two of the pairs are exceptionally small, considerably more so than the others, reducing their 'ability-to-be-put-on' status to 'impossible' (for my feet, a solid US 12, at least).

I'm happy, and will likely purchase again from sock manufacturer extraordinaire, James Fiallo.

This necklace fails on so many levels.

The biggest problem, as so many others have mentioned, is that the names just don't match. Wouldn't be so bad if it were a trinket like a geometric shape or an animal -- at least you could still use that. As it is, you have to get lucky to get the right name, but you still have to pay for it. I'm guessing there will be so many returns that this necklace will end up getting removed from the site.

I think this necklace has been mispackaged at production. For some reason, it seems like everyone is receiving a necklace with a different name than they ordered. I believe that it's because there is no actual label on the box, but a simple model number.

To be honest, I'm not sure if this is a problem with the manufacture at packaging or a problem with the seller's inventory control. Either way, I (like most others) received a different name than the one I ordered, and now I have to make a friend named Katie if I ever want to use this necklace.

Even assuming you are one of the lucky ones that actually receive the correct name . . . you will still be disappointed in the "dollar store" quality of this item.

The chain is weak and poorly made. It's very thin and the clasp is tricky (but it's not that different than other cheap necklaces). The name pendant itself is a very thin piece of metal that is probably plated in something gold-colored. I highly doubt they're using *real* gold considering the overall quality of everything else.

I think another reviewer mentioned this was something that you'd get out of a Cracker-Jackâ„¢ box, and they would be wrong -- Cracker-Jackâ„¢ wouldn't even stoop this low.

As it is, save your money and get a better quality necklace, because this one is a definite bust on all levels.

I ordered this watch in the green option, and it comes in a nice box and the entire watch band plus the face was protected with a thin film of plastic. When the plastic is removed that's when this watch really sparkles and it's true nature is brought to life. It has a stunning analog face with an emerald green starburst pattern background. Small rhinestones surround the face and give this watch a classy look. it is easy to read the time, and the size of the face alone (excluding the rhinestone rim) is slightly over 1.25" (3.3 cm). This watch keeps great time as it should and has what is called a deployment clasp. It folds over and snaps into place, then there are 2 little notches that are depressed to open the clasp to remove the watch.

My husband's wrist is 7.25" and the band was slightly too large for him. I only had to remove one link to make it a perfect fit. Another extremely nice feature of this watch is it came with the tool needed to remove the link! I have purchased many watches as I've been a watch nut for a long time, but have never had a watch come with the link remover tool. I had removed links from quite a few watches before so it was easy for me to do. I used the tool that came with the watch, and the pins removed easily so that was nice. The little user manual that comes with the watch does have a page on how to do this, but if you've never done it before I recommend just watching a couple short videos to see how it is done.

Overall this is a nice classy watch more on the dressy side, and looks great on my husband. We both love it! It keeps time well and has a band with a combination of satin and chrome finish. Last, it is affordable and is very giftable.

I am and RN married to and MD. Based on YouTube review by an RN, I purchased these. We have been wearing compression socks for years.

I wanted to love these socks. Awesome patterns and colors.

They would be awesome in practice if they were made of one piece of fabric, dyed multi-colored so that mmHg compression was consistent throughout the sock.

But thatâ€™s not the case. The striped and argyle socks are compromised of multiple pieces sewn together. The seams have a lot of excess fabric, nearly 1/2â€ high in some places. That causes higher compression wherever there is excess fabric. See the picture.

Same is true in footbed of black sock.

When I took the socks off, I had deeper indentations up and down and all around my calf. The color was more red than where just the sock fabric was. I have no edema or skin problemsâ€¦just normal skin.

I showed this to my MD spouse. Response? â€œWowâ€¦that could cause skin breakdown because of the pressure variance.â€

Note Dr. Schollâ€™s black 20-30mmHg compression sock at bottom of picture.. Solid piece of fabric. Seams are less prominent/dense. Thatâ€™s exactly why even these high compression socks do not cause the problems I experienced with this medium compression sock.

I contacted the company and explained my concern. Their reply?

â€œWhile we appreciate your feedback, we will not be taking the advice as we have many, many more customers who love our products and this is our business to run, not yours to tell us to shut down!â€

I was surprised at the reply. I never suggested they shut down. As a health care provider, I was concerned for others. I did encourage them to consider stop selling the product until the problem was addressed. Thatâ€™s not at all telling a business to shut down.

I suggested they use a model of their sock that doesnâ€™t have the problem. For clearly the company is capable of making socks without multiple seams with all the excess fabric on each seam: as in their rainbow sock.

At a minimum, I think they should let their customers know of the multiple pieces of fabric and untrimmed seams. I never would have purchased these had this been disclosed because the wearability outcome is completely predictable.

If the excess pressure from untrimmed seams doesnâ€™t cause any impact on your skin, then Iâ€™m glad they work for you.

For me, even though the rainbow socks are ok I prefer not to do business with companies that reply to a customer concern like this company did to mine. That is why I am returning even the rainbow socks.

This is a lovely piece, but I wish it were larger. I noticed that this seller offers very similar watches in a slightly larger size (this watch is 35 mm and the others are 38.5 mm). On most men, these others will look better. [[ASIN:B00ORJGIOC Findtime Mens Silver Luminous Tungsten Steel Quartz Wrist Watches]].

[[ASIN:B00ORJGEV4 Findtime Mens Silver Tungsten Steel Luxury Luminous Quartz Wrist Watches]]. Nonetheless, the description accurately described the dimensions, and for what it is, it has earned 5 stars.

First off, if you've looked at any of the other reviews, the big question on your mind is, "how fragile is this thing?" The seller makes a big deal in the description about not dropping the watch because it WILL shatter, not ifs, ands, or buts about it. As such, I haven't been willing to drop mine to find out. However, I TOOK A VERY SHARP KNIFE to the under side (just in case) of the watch band and tried hard to scratch it and couldn't. I'm satisfied that the band will keep looking brand new, so long as I (or my kids) don't drop it.

PROS:
- looks very handsome. The size is small enough for a woman, but when my wife tried it on, we both agreed it just looks masculine. That's impressive given how tiny it is by today's standards.
- sits very low to the wrist. This means it fits under ANY dress shirt cuff you've got.
- shockingly comfortable
- versatile (but mostly dressy)
- butterfly clasp is a cool feature
- easy to size (if you have the tools. I use one like this [[ASIN:B002Q8AJSM SE JT6218 5-Piece Watch Band Link Pin Tool Set]])
- Date window (warning: it is basically invisible to anyone with struggling eyesight)
- strong, multifaceted sapphire crystal (glass covering the face). This is perhaps my favorite part of the watch. I love how the different geometric cuts catch light. See my photos if that didn't make sense.

CONS:
- shows all fingerprints badly (face, bracelet, everywhere)
- tiny crown looks nice, but is awkward to turn when setting the time/date
- very small by modern men's watch trend standards.

WHAT I'D CHANGE:
- It's too small. I think this watch with a 40 mm face would be stunning!
- slightly bigger, more tactile crown

BOTTOM LINE: lovely watch, especially if you have a small wrist, but the bigger options above may be better for everyone else and whatever you do DON'T DROP IT!!!

When it comes to technology, I am a utilitarian. In other words, I don't want to spend money on a bunch of features that I don't really need. I remember wearing a watch just like this as a kid during the 1980s, and it served its purpose just fine. It also lasted a long, long time. So when I needed a cheap watch to wear while exercising, I decided to buy the same kind that worked for me all those years ago.

What you get here is a durable and tough watch that will tell you what time it is and beep when it's time to wake up. It'll also work underwater. That's about all it does. If this set of features is what you want, this watch is probably the absolute best value available.

If you like no-frills, plain-and-simple-tried-and-true products, sporting a watch like this is a good way to show it!

Since the wedding is outdoors with chairs on the lawn, women had been advised to wear flats, and in that case, this dress was going to have to be hemmed a full SIX INCHES (and would still hit the floor!) But there's only one seller, "OLRIK", and orders are fulfilled by Amazon.

Hence. Please check the name of seller before purchasing these products. levaca takes authenticty of product very seriously and will take legal action against all lmitation products and will further take possible action with Amazon.com." It seems the lack of attention to detail in the "Certificate of Achievement" is reflected in the product itself, which is obviously hit or miss.

I just got these today, but there were unanswered questions I had when reading the reviews so I thought I'd post them here.
First, the small size definitely fits a woman's 5-6 and a half shoe size. These "Cosmo colored" socks are not thin, but they are not as bulky as fleece socks either. The picture is realistic of what I received and how it fits the foot. I have small, wide (b-c) feet and these fit very well, with a little wiggle room side to side in the toes to make them comfortable. I have average legs and these fit very well on the ankles and calves. If you have wide lower legs, you might want to rethink these. They are NOT made to be slouchy in your fitted size (maybe if you go a size up?) The socks are not cushiony or extra soft, but they are comfortable. One review I read mentioned the rolled part of the sock in the picture. It puffs out like that when you wear them loose on your foot (which I like), but when they are off your feet the rolled section is flat...perhaps a different kind of stitching makes it that way. For looks these are a definite 10. For the money, yes it is a lot, but it is hard to find unusual clothing items without paying more. They are well made, and the fun, happy color combinations are wonderful, so ultimately the price value is up to you. For me, I will see how these wear over time and buy another pair. I will air dry them since in this size I wouldn't want them to shrink as other reviewers said. Maybe I'll splurge on a bigger size for a slouchier fit and machine dry them.

-The cord in the middle is the stretch elastic kind. It does seem relatively sturdy, but who knows how it will survive over time.

All told, these are a solid choice for the price. They feel about how one would expect for seven-ish bucks after shipping. For about the same cost as the sandalwood ones, I'd say go for it if you like the style

For transparency's sake, it seems prudent to admit that I am in no way a hat person. Actually, I kind of hate them. Always have. And I'm from Buffalo, NY, notorious winter capital of the Northeast, so imagine all the mornings my poor mother spent jamming knitwear on my head before I went out to wait for the schoolbus in the snow, shouting at me through the front window when I threw the hats into the yard, her voice lost to the relentless, driving wind. Later in life I'd decide headwear of any kind makes me look short (shut up; it's legit), and the cycle continued.

However, I shaved my head on a feminist whim a couple weeks ago, and I don't regret any part of it except not preparing for just. how. cold. my head would be. My hair must've been made out of fiberglass or something, because without it there for insulation I've been shivering like a chihuahua. A bald chihuahua. A week in and my lifetime hat boycott went down the drain (and probably got stuck in that clump of hair I mistakenly assumed wouldn't get caught just past the trap). Apparently proving your worth as a human being isn't dependent upon patriarchal beauty standards doesn't keep you warm.

Since I'm a hat n00b, I just searched for "knit hat." Obviously the results numbered in the zillions, so I just picked the first one that cost less than $15 and wasn't hideousâ€”two days later I was as warm and toasty as I'd been with a full head of cozy curls. In other words, this hat does its job. It's doing its job right now, actually, saving me from the scalp hypothermia I'd otherwise be battling in my 68-degree house. Honestly, I'm still not entirely sold on the concept. I got two additional knit caps in addition to this oneâ€”y'know, for varietyâ€”both from different companies, with different material and different linings, but the result is the same: my head is warm at the expense of its freedom. Eventually my scalp gets itchy and claustrophobic, likely due to a mix of my own neuroses and having very little hair to provide a buffer for my bare, never-been-exposed-to-anything-before skin. Maybe I'm just not used to wearing something on my head.

Either way, none of the hats are at fault. They're decent, hardworking hats. This one in particular has an excellent fleecy lining that feels like you're pulling a lamb onto your head, which feels a lot nicer than it sounds, I promise. The pattern on the knitted shell adds toughness in both look and feel, adding just enough flair to ensure you'll have a different hat than everyone else in the room without having the ugliest hat in the room. I can't speak on the other color options, but the charcoal grey I chose is the perfect dark dove shade to compliment my Goth Lite wardrobe.

My only issue is with the shape, which when worn creates two points on my head that look like a lowkey attempt at wearing a cat costume in public. Luckily it's roomy enough to allow for some reshaping at the back, but if you have a large skull you might want to carefully consider how concerned you are with people thinking you're storing a book under your hat.

I purchased this as a garden hat to keep the sun out of this old ladies eyes. First I found the hat on the small side. The brim is wide enough but the actual "cap" part that sits on your head wasn't wide enough. Kind of sat on top of my head so it would just fall off if I bent over. I do not have a large head by anyone's standard. I'm only 5'3". First I thought about returning it but decided to take a chance and do some alterations since I only wanted it for the garden. I removed the ribbon which is only attached in spots with dabs of glue...like the solder glue sticks you use for crafts. That helped just a tad because there were a few places that were soldered incorrectly and had created a "tuck". It was still a bit too small though. Finally I removed the strip of material that runs around the inside rim of the hat where the cap part attaches to the brim. That loosened it a little more...enough so I could get a more secure fit. There's a strap you can wear under your chin to keep the hat from falling off but I hate that in the heat. When I was done I just tied the ribbon back on the hat. I wouldn't buy another hat but I'll get enough use out of it. I suspect it will loosen up a bit too with wear. I also see a few spots on the inside of the hat were the straw weave is not secured properly. I'll use dabs of that craft glue to secure the ends of the straw weave so the hat doesn't start to fall apart.

All in all, I'm not impressed with the quality of this hat at all. If you have a truly small head, it might be fine but it's not for the average size head in my opinion.

UPDATE 11/01/16

These leggings also include a hidden pocket in the waistband, as indicated in the photos I provided. This pocket is pretty roomy and can adequately fit your keys or a small phone.

I have several pairs of Bentibo leggings now and like them all. However, these fit a bit smaller than the other pairs I own by this brand, despite advertising a "wider waistband." I am 5"1 and 110 lbs. and followed the size chart by ordering a Small. When I slid these on, I could hear one or two of the seams rip.. obviously not enough of the seams ripped to have any visible damage, but just a small critique.. I am not sure if more seams will continue to rip with continuous use, but the fact that I had to be careful when sliding this pair on is why I rated it 4 stars instead of 5. I could order a Medium instead, but I like where these leggings fall near my ankles (rather than drowning my legs as leggings normally do). All in all, these were the most flattering on my body of the Bentibo line, they just were a bit more snug than I expected.

QUALITY: I quality checked all of the seams on these pants to make sure that no seam was out of stitch, and everything looked great.
COLOR: The leggings are a heather gray with a black stripe down them (with a small orange and red Bentibo logo on the back).
SIZING: As mentioned above -- somewhat snugger fit than other Bentibo leggings, but not too noticeable to the point that I would return them.
LENGTH: Great length.. the size Small compliments those short in stature who might have trouble finding leggings that fit height-wise normally.

Overall...
PROS: Stylish, comfortable, flattering, spacious hidden pocket, flat seams to prevent chafing, a pretty comfortable fit, perfect length
CONS: Runs somewhat small (based on my own experience - might not be the same for you)

The belt came with a hole punch in case you need to add another hole to shorten the belt.  (The hole punch makes a round hole whereas the other pre-existing holes on the belt are oval shaped.  This different hole shape will be unnoticeable since the buckle hides the hole.) Note, the belt size does run large.  I wear a size 6/8 and ordered size Small due to the other reviews.  At its shortest, the belt measured 33 inches and was loose on my natural waist!  This size worked ok for pants that ride on the hips but I will probably punch another hole to make the belt shorter for those pants that sit on my natural waist.  There are 2 belt loops on the belt.  One is secured and stays next to the buckle.  The 2nd belt loop is loose and "float" around the belt.  It can easily come off when you hang it on a hook.  It would be much better if the loop wrapped around the belt tighter so it does not fall off.  Lastly, this belt is only 3/4" thick so it may be too thin for jeans. I'm actually pleasantly surprised. I've been shopping for a lightweight fleece jacket for a few weeks. I've looked at a lot of them online and in stores and decided to give this one a chance. I, honestly, didn't expect much. But the Colorado Timberline Jacket turns out to be exactly what I was looking for. The jacket is thick but surprisingly light weight. The fleece is soft. The zippers are made of nylon and work smoothly. I see no evidence of poor stitching or loose threads. It's perfect for a cool day in the 40s or 50s with a t-shirt and I would imagine it would be perfect on a colder day with a sweatshirt or sweater underneath. If you expect this to be a jacket that works when the weather is extremely cold you will be disappointed. It's made of 100% polyester so shrinkage shouldn't be an issue but it specifies cool water.

There seem to be a lot of questions about fit. I am a bit on the heavy side and generally wear shirts in size large. I ordered this in a large and it fits as though it were tailor-made for me. If you like a jacket a bit larger you'll want to go up a size from whatever you normally purchase.

Overall this is a very inexpensive product that's not cheap, with fit and finish of much more expensive items.

I ordered the black and grey version in 5X, and normally wear an XL or 2X in US sizes (5'3", 200lb). I was looking for a longer length zip-up jacket due to my large bust (32JJ, or 50" at fullest point) since a larger bust tends to eat up vertical space in tops and leaves them feeling super short in the front.

The fit for me is barely okay. On the good side, the sleeves are a good length though maybe a bit narrow in the bicep for me, and I can zip the jacket up alright. But... what's with the dual zippers? Like I get that the cross over of the fabric needed to be secured on the inside, but the interior zipper is identical in material and pull to the exterior one, and shows through the fabric since it runs along the right breast while the exterior zipper runs along the left. Morevoer, why does the interior zipper only go to about waist length and then stop? You literally have to zip both of these if you zip either of them, so the fashion-over-function-factor is strong with this jacket.

The pockets are also really weirdly placed. Way off around my sides rather than sitting on the front. This is probably a relic of really poor pattern scaling, as someone who was narrower in profile but wider from the front would probably find them well placed. But for a pretty typical round-shaped person in this size range, my hands are resting basically on the small of my back with my hands in these pockets.

Another indicator of poor pattern scaling is the neckhole, which is humongous in this size. I hate when stuff touches my neck, so the v-neck on this was actually one of the reasons I purchased. But in this size the plackets of this jacket cross pretty much at the bridge of my bra. If I wasn't wearing a shirt underneath, I'd call it inappropriately low cut for a super casual office setting in a progressive/liberal/nudity-legal part of the world. Put another way, the top of the zipper only goes to just below the fullest point of my bust, so... in cold weather this will need a few scarves, to say the least.

I don't know if I'd recommend this jacket to other women - plus size women - similar in shape to myself (larger belly and bust, smaller hips and thighs). It's particularly straight cut through the upper half so I don't get a lot of waist definition from my bust and am a little bit compressed, which I'm used to. On the lower half though the pockets are right along the "flare out" for hip shaping, whereas the banded bottom sits right below my belly and on my narrow hips; this makes the pockets stick out funny and makes my hips appear "lumpy", all while accentuating my front belly roll. Why? Because this sucker is LONG. The wide banded bottom hugs the underside of my butt cheeks.

TL;DR: I was looking for a longer sweatshirt with a lower neckline, but the 5X size of this jacket has more than 5x the length and 5x the neck hole because of cheaply scaled patterns during manufacturing. Beware of funny pockets if you have narrow hips, a short waist, or more than just a little tummy chub.

I purchased this watch because I've been eyeing this (and it's metal/chrome counterpart) for years now. This is all of the information I needed on a smartwatch screen. After my last apple watch bit the dust, I decided to go for an old-fashioned wristwatch. I am also joining the US Navy and needed a black wristwatch with an alarm - they sell them at basic, but I want to already be familiar with my watch beforehand. This fit the bill perfectly.

For $10, this thing is amazing. Setting it is a breeze. You program the month into the watch so it knows how many days there are, so you don't have to reset it monthly like many mechanical watches that show the date. So you literally just set everything once and you're set.

I love how light it is - I'll probably end up sleeping with this thing on. I am a tall guy and the face is a bit small, however the information is clearly present and easy to see.

My only complaint is the light. It lights up the left side of the screen, but the 1/3 in the middle and 1/3 to the right are still pretty dark. I can use the light and see the info okay in the dark, so it does serve its purpose. It could be better though, but this is where I'm like "I paid $10 for this thing", so over all not an issue.

DEFINITELY recommended. May not be pretty, but I've always been a "function over fashion" sort of person, and this watch is amazing.

Highly recommend, especially if you need something for military service.

I bought these for a camping trip and could not be more pleased with how they worked out. Despite their deceptively casual appearance, they're very well-suited to outdoor activities and I was able to test them in pretty rough conditions. Our 6-mile hike was quite steep and rocky, and it started pouring halfway, yet I had no trouble at all! These boots have some nice lift, but since the heels are slightly wider around the bottom, I felt perfectly balanced. They lace up all the way, so my ankles felt extremely supported, and they have fantastic grip without any annoying gaps on the bottom for pebbles to get lodged inside. Even in the rain, I never lost my footing at all, and my feet stayed totally dry. The textured laces remained firmly tied, and there are several reflective strips on the front and back for added safety. I was really impressed with how these performed all around.

That hike was the first time I wore the boots at length, so I expected at least some blisters, but I was actually fine! I found them quite comfortable and true to size. I'm a consistent size 7 and they fit perfectly with just enough toe room. The insoles are pretty firm and they have decent arch support. They're pretty thick and hearty, so they don't breathe super well and can get a bit warm in higher temps. They're very versatile though, and I found that I can wear them differently and pair them with various socks to get exactly the comfort I need for specific situations.

For the long hike, the boots felt great with the added cushion of my padded outdoor socks, and the moisture-wicking helped my feet stay cool. I also prefer higher socks when I'm lacing them up fully and tightly for maximum stability, just so they don't rub my ankles. For lighter activities, I don't bother with the top two hooks and just knot them underneath so they fit more like regular sneakers. That way, they're perfectly comfy with any socks for basically any activity. I'll even throw them on to run to the store! Ultimately, these function fabulously no matter what I'm doing, so I'll get tons of use out of them. They seem high quality and well-constructed, and I'm sure they'll last a long time.

Before I try a product, or ever order it for that matter, I like to look at the reviews on Amazon to see what people like and dislike. I noticed everyone mentioned that these run small. That is because the sizing is Asian. If you pick just the number that is an Asian size. If you pick the one that says â€œAsian #/US #â€ than the US size number is accurate. I wear a size 31 waist and I ordered a size Asian 34/US 33. The waist did indeed fit like a 33 waist. The rest of the pant fit perfectly. The extra waist is not a bid deal as I can use a belt, but if I could do it over I would order the next size down.

Another reviewer complained that the pants fade after the first time washing. I took a picture before and after washing and drying the pants and I did not notice any fading. I am sure they will fade over time as the colors are very dark and vivid, but all my clothes fade with time. The pants feel great. I love the inner fleece liner. They appear to be well made. These are great for cold conditions. I wish the outer material was not cotton as these would make great snow pants. I have not tried these in snow as I live in Texas, but plan on it eventually. These pants have several pockets.

This is a high quality, 100% genuine leather belt. You will know it is genuine leather the second that you open the box. The smell of real leather is unmistakable. If you need more than that for proof it is also stamped with 100% genuine leather stamp. The belt is 1 1/2" wide and is solid black. On one side of the belt there is a pattern of repeating diamonds with a single wave that runs through the pattern. It is not a pattern that is over the top or obnoxious. It is classy and looks great with slacks or jeans. If you prefer a flat look, you can simply reverse the buckle and have a solid black non-patterned belt. The buckle is very masculine. It has a sheen to the space gray color but is not glossy. The buckle is reversible with the removal of a single brad with a flat head fitting on the back side.

I ordered this belt in a size 36". When I measure the belt from the leather at the buckle to the last hole available for use, it is exactly 36". I wear a size 34 on most every pair of pants I buy. They fit me a little loose as I can wear a size 33 comfortably, but it is not a size I can find easily. If I measure my actual waste or wear I wear my pants, my measurement is actually 34.5". I only go into detail because there can be huge variation when it comes to belts. When I put this belt on, I use the 2nd to last hole available. This is the way I like my belt to fit. I don't mind if they are a little longer, but I do know most of my friends prefer them longer.

I received a discount for providing my honest review of this belt. It fit my waist perfectly. It has a nice design that is not to gaudy or can be worn without it. The buckle is very masculine and has a very nice color. Finally, the smell of 100% genuine leather is unmistakable and reminds you of the great quality. This belt had no negatives in my opinion.

I am very disappointed in this watch, the F-91W.

I have owned a different watch, the Casio W-71 for many years, and find it to be a versatile watch, but the band just broke (as they do after several years). I purchased the F-91W awhile back as a future replacement, but found it lacking seriously when I had to use it. I would have sent it back, but considering the cost of shipping, it was not worth it.

The features are scaled back compared to the W-71. There is no count-down timer, which I use almost daily. The button that cycles through the features goes through the "change time," making it easy to change the time by mistake. (The button layout is not convenient for someone who uses the different features multiple times daily, but I concede that may be my bias.) I also use the feature to set an alarm for a specific date (the one day I have to catch a plane at 6 am), so I do not forget and get awakened at 4 am for the next few days. There are more limitations and flaws in addition to these I have listed.

Pros:
cheap
its a Casio

Cons:
too easy to change the time by mistake
limted features
no month on date, just the day (fine, my pet peeve)
no count down timer
single alarm mode
(button layout not as easy to use)

The W-71 is about twice the cost, but well worth it. I am going to find a replacement band (or two) for my old one, and put this F-91W back in a drawer.

Spend the extra $10 for a much better watch. Stock up on replacement bands at Wal-Mart or such and it will last for many years.

I'm snapping up as many colors of these as I can find for the right price. Just a great all around travel and outdoor hat. So lightweight, breathable and stow-able. My backpack never goes on a hike without one of these caps packed inside! This is really a five star item but here's the deal why I didn't quite go there: There is some variation in the sizing, i.e. I ordered two of these in the same size but one had to be returned because it was too large as opposed to the other one that fit. There is also a noticeable difference in how this model fits from the Radar Storm cap. The two caps look nearly identical but the fit of the crown is MUCH more shallow on the Storm versions whereas the regular version offers a fuller and deeper crown . Lastly, as many of the other reviewers stated these run really big. So to be direct, I don't think there are too many men who can realistically wear the XL unless you have really, really, super large heads. I learned this from experience by having to return an XL for a L. The L was spot on.

I'm not sure if OR is still making these because of the variation in availability and pricing but I'm sure glad I've picked up a few for a fair enough price.

Objective - I was looking for the following:
--Leather
--Backpack / briefcase (vertical and horizontal) capabilty
--Durable construction (zippers and seams)
--Classic overall look and feel

I was apprehensive when I first ordered this, as the photos on Amazon were inconclusive. I ordered two leather backpacks so I could evaluate both.

this one is the winner hands-down.

I have found few bags that effectively double as both a comfortable backpack (for plane travel, etc), and for legitimate business use (hold it like a briefcase & not have it look like a backpack). this one nails it.

The construction is durable. the seams hold well. the straps for the backpack - i was concerned this would be a spartan leather strap that would be uncomfortable to wear -- but that's not the case at all.

Advice:

--There are so many zippers and pockets when you first get it, it will take you a while to explore all the options and opportunities.
--the briefcase handles, for example, zip out and stash away. there are pockets within pockets - some work better for briefcase use, others for packpack use.
--There are 2 puzzling leather belts on either side of the top of the backpack. I could not figure out exactly what they were for so - critical advice: I combined the 2 belts in to a large belt, and I use it as a handle on the top of the backpack (like most non-leather laptop backpacks have). the loops that this attaches to seem very securely sewn on, so it does not appear to be damaging the backpack from using this way. I assume these loops were designed to offer different options for how to pick up the pack when its in backpack-mode.
--the briefcase handle pockets actually provide very good pockets for other uses. I keep some snack bars and 5 hour energies stashed in that pocket.
--Note: the laptop pocket will only velcro-closed for smaller laptops (not sure the dimensions). However, my larger laptop (with the number pad on the keyboard), will still fit perfectly in this pocket and the bag zips closed. I just cant use the velcro. that's one potential improvement is making the laptop velcro higher so a bigger laptop will fit.
--The briefcase pocket works well for stashing my laptop cord and other items that need a large space - but that if they accidentally fell out because I forgot to zip the pocket, would not be catastrophic (unlike the laptop). anyway - this is just a preference for how I've used the various pockets.

this provides excellent functionality, seems durable and well-made, and has a classic slightly distressed leather feel to it. Looks like you could have owned it for 20 years.

Highly recommend.

GIFT: this would be an excellent gift for anyone starting a new professional job. we tend to be particular about our briefcase choices, so I would not assume someone would just swap out of their existing briefcase - but for someone out of school for example, this would be a "safe" business accessory for a professional job.

Update Jan-2019: I wear these daily, almost exclusively indoors, and the sole has hardly any wear. But after approximately a year and half the foam padded insole started to break down in the balls of the feet. I wish the insole had lasted a bit longer, but regardless - I am ordering another pair. I like them that much.

Original Review: The build quality of these sandals is top notch. These aren't cheap rubber sandals. The sole is thick and sturdy.

The padded insole is quite comfortable. And it has good arch, metatarsal and heel support which most sandals lack. So comfy on my relatively flat feet.

My one concern is that the insole's soft memory foam will break down eventually. But that remains to be seen. As it stands right now the insole is like I said, super comfy.

The insole is fabric-covered (unlike most other sandals) and is nice and comfortable. One note: If you plan on wearing the sandals with socks (as I often do, I'll admit!) you will slide around on the insole a bit. So these sandals may be best suited for bare feet.

The only negative is that the sandals (due to their solid build quality) are a bit heavier than any other other sandals I've ever owned. So they take some getting used to with the extra weight on your feet. Sounds trivial, but believe me when you're walking around all day you do notice it. Not a huge issue, but something to note.

Overall though, probably the best built sandals you can buy.

Good looking watch with pleasant aesthetics. Although the silver hands are similar in color to the face, they are surprisingly easy read considering the low contrast. Could do without the buckle clasp on the leather strap though, A clamping clasp would be much better. Those buckles on a leather strap tend to prematurely damage and wear out the strap. Replaced the strap with a 23mm black silicone Archer strap; looks fantastic and contrasts nicely with the light colored face. This is a heavy watch and what's good about the silicone band is the watch stays put where I like it; just above the pisiform bone. Don't like a loose watch where it can get damaged, and I have to fiddle to see the time as it flops around loose on my wrist. Accuracy is excellent as is almost always the case with a quartz movement. The date window is too small. The window perimeter casts a shadow on the date digits which makes the date more difficult to read.
UPDATE: After less than a few days of use, the chrono start button has a problem. Fails to stop and then restart to continue a timing. NOT GOOD! I thought maybe the watch mechanism was defective. however, it seems the oblong buttons can "misfire" or not misfire. Pressing the button closer to the 12o'clock and the chrono fails to stop and start properly, but if the button is pressed below center and closer to the crown it works fine. I have TWO of this same model watch and the other one works fine. It appears to be an alignment problem with the chrono start button and the mechanism. NOT GOOD! Definitely a QUALITY CONTROL PROBLEM since this is a brand NEW watch. Sorry but going to have to knock the stars down on this VERY nice appearance watch. It is just absolutely UNACCEPTABLE to send out a $650 watch with buttons that DO NOT WORK properly, and there are only TWO!

My earring holes are somewhat high on my ears and I have larger lobes so these do not fit me at all, which would be one of my biggest complaints. They do fit nicely on my 3 ear old who has much lower holes and thinner lobes. They are a bit thick, but not so thick that they look strange on her, which is nice. A thing I have found with my 3 year old is that she loses backs off her normal stud earrings, so a very nice thing about these hoops are they are one solid piece that clips together and is not pulled apart easily. This makes it almost impossible for her to lose an earring, which is great. The colors are very bright and beautiful, and she has been wearing the blue set for a week without any noticeable wear to the patina of the earring. Also the fact that they are stainless steel is great, any professional piercing parlor will encourage you, and normally starts their customers off wearing stainless steel jewelry. The stainless steel does not cause any reaction or irritation and is easy to keep clean. Make sure these will fit your lobes, and other than that its a pretty good product. I've been a fan of "fit-over" sunglasses for many years. I find them easier to use and less expensive than prescription sunglasses, but having to park them on top of my head when not in use made them prone to falling off, in addition to giving me a "six-eyed" look that even I didn't like. So when I saw these sunglasses that both fit over and flip up I had to try them.

I have a rather large head (size 8) so my concerns were that they would clamp too tight, be too heavy and that having two sets of nose pieces resting on my nose would be uncomfortable. None have been the case, although they are a little heavier than other fitovers I've worn. The nosepieces of the sunglasses rest neatly in front of my eyeglasses for a perfect fit. They sit a little bit higher on my face than other fitovers I've owned, but they seem to provide good protection from the sun from all angles.

For looks these are definitely not Ray-Bans but they have a certain high-tech charm. They're great for outdoor exercise and the beach, and I imagine they'd also be good for baseball or softball.

At least one of the vendors was offering free returns so that's an option if you're unsure about the fit For me they're great, and I bought three pairs in the various shades.
